subject.title: active-memory plugin causes session looping when model treats injected context as prompt (2026.7.1)

question: Should active-memory retain its current dynamic user-prompt prepend contract and fix only a demonstrated session scheduler path, or should OpenClaw define a new compatibility-gated delivery contract for recalled context?
rationale: The existing hook contract intentionally distinguishes dynamic user-context prepends from static system context, while the report proposes alternatives that could change provider behavior, caching, and plugin compatibility; source inspection alone cannot choose that product contract safely.

options.title: Trace then narrowly repair
options.body: First reproduce the repeated-session trigger on current main and repair the concrete scheduler or recursion path while retaining the existing dynamic-context contract.

options.title: Define capability-gated recall
options.body: Introduce an explicitly supported compatibility policy for models that cannot safely consume recalled context, with clear upgrade behavior and focused provider coverage.

options.title: Redesign prompt delivery
options.body: Adopt a new prompt-delivery API only after validating its provider, cache, and plugin-SDK consequences across supported runtimes.

recommendation.title: Trace then narrowly repair
recommendation.body: First reproduce the repeated-session trigger on current main and repair the concrete scheduler or recursion path while retaining the existing dynamic-context contract.

likelyOwner.reason: Their related work on the system-context plugin-hook option is the closest evidenced ownership trail for a possible delivery-contract decision.
